data.title: The Divinka – Veľký vrch educational trail
data.excerpt: Our Hradiská civic association, together with the village of Divinka and a number of partners, has created a new educational trail at the Veľký vrch hillfort in Divinka. Seven information panels lead from the centre of the village up to the summit area of the hillfort and tell the story of the site and of the most important archaeological cultures that occupied it.
data.metaTitle: The Divinka – Veľký vrch educational trail
data.metaDescription: An educational trail to the Veľký vrch hillfort at Divinka: seven information panels on the history of the hillfort and the cultures that occupied it.

keyFacts.label: Educational trail
keyFacts.value: Runs from the centre of the village of Divinka right up to the summit area of the hillfort, with 7 information panels on the history of the hillfort and on the archaeological cultures

keyFacts.label: Partners
keyFacts.value: the Hradiská civic association, the village of Divinka, the Institute of Archaeology of the Slovak Academy of Sciences, the Považské Museum in Žilina, the Veľký vrch joint-ownership community, Hradisko Divinka, the Pontis Foundation and the Kia Motors.

keyFacts.label: Academic supervision
keyFacts.value: The texts were corrected by PhDr. Gabriel Fusek, CSc. (the Institute of Archaeology); unique photographs of the finds were provided by Mgr. Andrea Slaná (the Považské Museum in Žilina)

keyFacts.label: Protection of the site
keyFacts.value: The hillfort is a national cultural monument (NKP) — installing the panels required administrative proceedings by the Regional Monuments Board in Žilina

keyFacts.label: Planned extension
keyFacts.value: Once the ongoing archaeological excavation is finished, a further 2 panels with the results of the latest fieldwork will be added at Veľký vrch

Andrea Slaná.

children.text: Our Hradiská civic association, together with the village of Divinka, the Institute of Archaeology of the Slovak Academy of Sciences, the Považské Museum in Žilina, the Veľký vrch joint-ownership community, Hradisko Divinka and with financial assistance from the Pontis Foundation and the Kia Motors Slovakia Endowment Fund, has created a new educational trail at the Veľký vrch hillfort in Divinka, about the history of the hillfort and the most important archaeological cultures that occupied it.

The educational trail will take you from the centre of the village right up to the summit area of the hillfort, and during your journey our seven information panels will tell you a great many interesting things about our distant past. While the panels were being prepared, thanks to the great helpfulness of the Institute of Archaeology (PhDr. Gabriel Fusek, CSc.), which corrected all the texts used with a strict eye both in scholarly and in linguistic terms, and of the Považské Museum in Žilina (Mgr. Andrea Slaná), who provided us with unique photographs of finds from earlier excavations at the hillfort, as well as to other collaborators, we managed to achieve an educational trail of high quality both in scholarly and in visual terms, containing a number of hitherto unpublished pictures and pieces of information, which we trust will interest all lovers of history.

blocks.alt: The Divinka – Veľký vrch educational trail

children.text: The opening of the educational trail took place on 31 August 2014 as part of the Staroslovanská Divinka event. Čendo, a representative of our association, ceremonially christened the whole educational trail here, and then all those present set out in the footsteps of our ancestors to acquaint themselves with all seven panels of the educational trail. Expert commentary of high quality was provided by the archaeologist Mgr. Andrea Slaná.

Once the archaeological excavation at the hillfort is finished, we will add a further 2 panels at Veľký vrch, and these will cover the results of the very latest fieldwork that is currently under way at the hillfort.

Finally, thanks are due to the staff of the Regional Monuments Board in Žilina, who dealt with the administrative proceedings for permission to install the panels (which in this case had to take place, since the hillfort is a national cultural monument) as a priority and within shortened deadlines. 
 Do all come and see our educational trail, which we hope will have a long life, just like our other panels...
